| 23 | PANGOLIN: Fuzzing Multilingual IoT Firmware with LLM-Driven Code Analysis | 2026 | LLM-driven cross-language code analysis for semantic-aware fuzzing; extracts hidden backend interfaces and generates parameter specifications using LLM agents with response-driven feedback correction | USENIX Security 2026 | LLM-Driven Fuzzing for IoT Firmware | None | PANGOLIN proposes an LLM-driven approach to fuzz multilingual IoT firmware by automatically extracting backend interfaces (including those hidden from the frontend) and generating semantically correct input parameter specifications. It uses an LLM agent to perform cross-language code analysis across C, JavaScript, PHP, Python, and Lua, enabling semantics-aware fuzzing that explores deeper code paths. Evaluated on 12 multilingual IoT devices from 8 major manufacturers, PANGOLIN discovered 2,856 backend interfaces (1,793 hidden from the frontend) and 68 zero-day vulnerabilities including command injection, XSS, information leaks, and DoS — achieving 2.96× more vulnerabilities than the SOTA tool LABRADOR. | Tested on 12 real-world IoT devices from 8 vendors. Found 2,856 interfaces (1,793 hidden) and 68 zero-day vulnerabilities. Outperformed LABRADOR by 2.96×; 45 of 68 vulnerabilities were in hidden interfaces vs. only 4 for EAGLEYE. All reported to vendors; 31 vulnerability IDs assigned. |
| 57 | FirmAgent: Leveraging Fuzzing to Assist LLM Agents with IoT Firmware Vulnerability Discovery | 2026 | Hybrid Fuzzing + LLM Agent: fuzzing identifies source points, LLM does taint propagation, PoC auto-generation | NDSS 2026 | Hybrid Fuzzing + LLM Static Analysis | 15 | FirmAgent is the first hybrid solution that leverages fuzzing to assist LLM agents in finding vulnerabilities in IoT firmware. It addresses the key limitations of both static analysis (high false positives, no PoC) and dynamic fuzzing (high false negatives). Fuzzing accurately identifies taint source points, then an LLM agent performs context-aware taint propagation analysis, and another generates PoC testcases. Tested on 14 real-world IoT router firmware, it found 182 vulnerabilities with 91% precision, including 140 0-day vulnerabilities and 17 CVEs. | Evaluated on 14 real-world IoT router firmware. Achieved 91% precision (182/200 confirmed), compared to EmTaint (37%), HermeScan (33%), Greenhouse (40%). Discovered 140 previously unknown vulnerabilities, 17 with CVE IDs. Ablation study showed removing fuzzing information drops precision from 91% to 74%. PoC auto-generation success rate: 91.8%. |
| 59 | Energy-Efficient Multi-LLM Reasoning for Binary-Free Zero-Day Detection in IoT Firmware | 2025 | Tri-LLM Architecture (LLaMA + DeepSeek + GPT-4o) + Energy-Aware Symbolic Load Model, no binary/firmware access needed | arXiv preprint (arXiv:2512.19945) | Binary-Free Zero-Day Detection | 17 | This paper proposes a binary-free, architecture-agnostic solution for zero-day vulnerability detection in IoT firmware, addressing scenarios where firmware is encrypted, stripped, or inaccessible. Unlike methods requiring binary visibility or emulation, it uses only high-level descriptors and a tri-LLM reasoning architecture combining LLaMA, DeepSeek, and GPT-4o. It formally derives mathematical foundations (monotonicity, divergence, energy-risk coupling) and incorporates computational signatures and energy-aware modeling. Simulation shows high exposure conditions increase zero-day likelihood by 20-35% across models, with GPT-4o showing strongest cross-layer correlations. | Simulation-based evaluation across multi-LLM pipeline. High exposure conditions increased predicted zero-day likelihood by 20-35%. GPT-4o demonstrated strongest cross-layer correlations and highest sensitivity. Energy and divergence metrics significantly predicted elevated risk. Formal mathematical proofs establish monotonicity, divergence, and energy-risk coupling properties. Novel contribution: works without any binary/code/firmware access. |
